newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures fall as cash market stays weak.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures fall as cash market stays weak.

text.p: An overbought condition on an expected rise in cash prices failed to materialize and CME lumber futures fell early despite sharply higher to limit advances on Thursday, traders said.

Futures fell at the start as there was no carryover demand from Thursday's gains and selling developed on quoted lower cash prices. A flurry of activity in cash markets Thursday sparked concern that cash prices had turned up, pushing July futures up the limit, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $384 per tbf, down $4 from midweek and $13 under last weeks level.
At 0931 CDT, futures stood $8.00 to $1.50 lower with limitless May off most at $391.50 and July off $1.90 at $392.60 per tbf.
